title: Align ExitWorktree tool with the TS baseline
objective: Implement all ExitWorktree improvements identified by the per-tool subagent report so the Go clone matches the original TypeScript tool in public contract, runtime logic, robustness, state lifecycle, and tests.

context.problem: Go ExitWorktree has the visible keep/remove action names and basic git worktree removal flow, but it is not fully aligned with the TS reference. The biggest divergences are structured output, current-session scoping, fail-closed change detection, restoration of session/tool state, hook-based worktree lifecycle, tmux lifecycle, destructive-permission metadata, cleanup failure semantics, strict input validation, and real-git regression coverage. Several Go helpers exist toward parity, such as persisted WorktreeState, cache invalidator hooks, ResponseJSON, and discovery metadata, but ExitWorktree does not yet wire them into the same runtime contract as TS.

parallelization_notes: Can be assigned to an implementation subagent after listed dependencies are available. Avoid running concurrently with another task that owns the same files.

improvement_points.title: Go returns free-form text instead of the TS structured output object
improvement_points.description: TS declares an output schema and returns { data: ... } containing action, originalCwd, worktreePath, worktreeBranch, tmuxSessionName, discardedFiles, discardedCommits, and message. The UI renderer consumes those fields. Go ExitWorktree returns plain ToolResult.Content strings such as 'Worktree session ended (kept)' or 'Worktree removed and branch deleted', with no JSON object or stable typed fields. Go has a ResponseJSON helper elsewhere, but ExitWorktree does not use it.

improvement_points.title: Current-session scope guard is broader in Go because ExitWorktree reloads repo-wide persisted state
improvement_points.description: TS gates ExitWorktree on getCurrentWorktreeSession(), with an explicit message that manually created worktrees and worktrees from a previous session are not touched unless the session has been restored into currentWorktreeSession. Go, when inactive in memory, calls canonicalGitRoot and loadFromDisk before deciding no session exists. That repo-wide .claude/worktree-session.json path lets a later process/session exit state created elsewhere, which is a broader lifecycle surface than the TS current-session guard.

improvement_points.title: No-active-session and invalid-input semantics differ from TS validation
improvement_points.description: TS uses validateInput to reject no-active-session with result:false and errorCode 1 before call() runs, and zod enum validation rejects invalid action at schema validation time. Go checks for an active session before validating action and returns a non-error success ToolResult '(no worktree session active)' when inactive. As a result, an invalid action with no active state is reported as no-op success in Go, while TS would reject the action or active-session validation through the tool validation path.

improvement_points.title: Remove safety does not use TS originalHeadCommit baseline and does not fail closed on unknown state
improvement_points.description: TS countWorktreeChanges fails closed when git status fails, originalHeadCommit is missing, or rev-list fails; it counts commits with originalHeadCommit..HEAD. Go WorktreeState does not record originalHeadCommit. The remove guard ignores the git status error, only checks non-empty combined output, and unmergedCommits compares against origin/<branch> or origin/HEAD. If no candidate upstream can be verified, Go returns ok=false and proceeds as if there were no commits. This is materially different from TS, which treats unknown state as unsafe unless discard_changes is true.

improvement_points.title: ExitWorktree does not restore the broader session/tool runtime state that TS restores
improvement_points.description: TS restoreSessionToOriginalCwd resets Shell cwd, originalCwd, conditionally projectRoot and hook snapshots, clears persisted worktree state, system prompt sections, memory-file caches, and plans directory cache. Go ExitWorktree only conditionally os.Chdir's the process and calls InvalidateWorktreeCaches, but ExitWorktree owns only WorktreeState and cannot update BashTool.CWD, RuntimeScope, PlanState, BackgroundTasks, TodoStore, CronStore, file allowed dirs, or MCP settings. RegistryDeps.UpdateSessionContext has the needed shape, but it is not wired into ExitWorktree. The cache invalidator registry has no production registrations in the searched code.

improvement_points.title: Hook-based worktree exit/removal is not equivalent
improvement_points.description: TS supports hook-based worktree sessions: createWorktreeForSession records hookBased state and cleanupWorktree delegates removal to WorktreeRemove. Go declares a hook bridge and EnterWorktree can call WorktreeCreate in non-git directories, but that branch returns immediately without recording an active WorktreeState. WorktreeState has no HookBased field, and ExitWorktree always uses git worktree remove and git branch -D for action='remove'. The default Go bridge is also a no-op in-memory placeholder unless runtime code replaces it.

improvement_points.title: Tmux session state is not tracked, killed, or reported like TS
improvement_points.description: TS WorktreeSession can carry tmuxSessionName. ExitWorktree keep leaves the tmux session running and returns a reattach note, while remove kills the tmux session before cleanup. Go only has a best-effort maybeRenameTmuxWindow helper during EnterWorktree; WorktreeState has no tmux session name, ExitWorktree does not kill tmux on remove, and keep output cannot include the TS reattach note.

improvement_points.title: Input-level destructive classification for remove is missing in Go
improvement_points.description: TS marks ExitWorktree as shouldDefer, classifies action='remove' as destructive, and passes the action to the auto-classifier. Go has discovery metadata marking ExitWorktree deferred, but the generic Tool interface has no isDestructive/toAutoClassifierInput equivalent and ExitWorktree does not expose input-sensitive destructive metadata to the permission layer. The remove path can delete a worktree and branch after discard_changes=true without a TS-equivalent classifier surface.

improvement_points.title: Partial cleanup and failure semantics differ from TS
improvement_points.description: TS cleanupWorktree catches and logs git remove/branch-delete failures, clears currentWorktreeSession and activeWorktreeSession, and ExitWorktree still returns a structured success message after cleanupWorktree returns. Go returns IsError and leaves state uncleared if git worktree remove fails, while branch deletion failure is returned as a special plain-text success and state is cleared. Go also deletes the branch immediately, while TS waits briefly for git locks before branch deletion.

improvement_points.title: Strict object validation and discard_changes schema text are not equivalent
improvement_points.description: TS uses z.strictObject and describes discard_changes as required when remove would discard uncommitted files or unmerged commits. Go's JSONSchema has the same top-level property names, but no additionalProperties:false representation, parseInputOrError uses json.Unmarshal which ignores unknown fields, and the discard_changes description mentions only uncommitted changes. Go also performs manual action validation after inactive-state handling.

improvement_points.title: Worktree keep/remove analytics with changed-file and commit counts are missing
improvement_points.description: TS emits tengu_worktree_kept and tengu_worktree_removed with mid_session, commits, and changed_files after recounting at execution time. Go ExitWorktree does not emit an equivalent analytics event or metadata, and because it lacks originalHeadCommit-based counting it cannot currently match the TS counts.

improvement_points.title: Go tests do not lock the TS parity contract for real git removal, structured output, state restoration, hooks, or tmux
improvement_points.description: Existing Go tests cover simple state clearing, no-active success, substring markers, fake non-git paths, and a cache invalidator callback. They do not use a real git fixture to verify originalHeadCommit..HEAD safety, unknown-state fail-closed behavior, structured JSON output, restored tool-local runtime state, hook-based WorktreeRemove, tmux kill/keep notes, or TS cleanup failure semantics. Several tests currently encode Go-specific behavior that conflicts with TS, such as no-active being non-error and remove failures returning IsError.

implementation_subtasks.title: Return TS-shaped structured ExitWorktree results and align no-active/invalid-action outcomes
acceptance_criteria: action='keep' returns parseable JSON with action, originalCwd, worktreePath, optional worktreeBranch, optional tmuxSessionName, and message.
action='remove' returns parseable JSON with action, originalCwd, worktreePath, optional worktreeBranch, discardedFiles, discardedCommits, and message.
No active session is reported as a tool error/validation failure equivalent to TS, not as successful '(no worktree session active)' prose.
Invalid action is rejected even when there is no active worktree state.
Existing prose-scraping tests are replaced or supplemented with structured field assertions.
implementation_subtasks.notes: Introduce an ExitWorktree response struct mirroring the TS output schema and return it through ResponseJSON or the repo's preferred structured-result helper. Validate action before inactive-state handling, return TS-equivalent tool-error semantics for no active session, and preserve exact fields for keep/remove including discardedFiles/discardedCommits when available.

implementation_subtasks.title: Constrain ExitWorktree to TS-equivalent current-session worktree state
acceptance_criteria: A fresh process in the same repo cannot ExitWorktree a prior session merely because .claude/worktree-session.json exists.
An explicitly restored/resumed session can ExitWorktree after the worktree path still exists.
Stale persisted state whose path no longer exists is cleared without acting on filesystem paths.
Concurrent or separate session IDs do not share a single active WorktreeState unless intentionally restored.
implementation_subtasks.notes: Replace or scope the repo-wide loadFromDisk behavior so ExitWorktree only operates on worktree state associated with the current session, matching TS currentWorktreeSession/restoreWorktreeSession semantics. If persisted recovery remains required, make it sessionId-keyed and only restore through an explicit resume path.

implementation_subtasks.title: Implement fail-closed TS change counting with originalHeadCommit baseline
acceptance_criteria: A clean worktree with originalHeadCommit and no changes can be removed without discard_changes.
Uncommitted files block remove without discard_changes and report the file count.
Commits on originalHeadCommit..HEAD block remove without discard_changes even when origin/HEAD would not reveal them.
Missing originalHeadCommit or failing git status/rev-list blocks remove without discard_changes with an unknown-state message.
discard_changes=true proceeds and returns discardedFiles/discardedCommits counts based on the execution-time recount.
implementation_subtasks.notes: Add OriginalHeadCommit to WorktreeState/persistedWorktreeState, populate it when entering/creating a git worktree, and implement countWorktreeChanges(path, originalHeadCommit) with TS semantics: git status failure, missing baseline, or rev-list failure returns unknown and remove without discard_changes refuses. Use the same counts for output and analytics.

implementation_subtasks.title: Restore registry/runtime state and concrete caches when exiting a worktree
acceptance_criteria: After keep/remove, BashTool.CWD and PowerShellTool.CWD point at originalDir when TS would setCwd(originalCwd).
RuntimeScope, PlanState, BackgroundTasks, TodoStore, CronStore, TeamManager, file allowed dirs, and MCP settings are retargeted consistently through the registry restoration path.
System prompt, memory-file, plans, hooks/settings-equivalent caches have production invalidators registered and are invoked on exit.
Worktree keep/remove analytics fire with mid_session=true and changed file/commit counts once TASK-003 is available.
Tests prove tool-local state changes without relying solely on os.Getwd.
implementation_subtasks.notes: Inject a session-context restoration callback or dependency bundle into ExitWorktree so keep/remove can update the same runtime surfaces TS updates: shell CWD, project/runtime scope, plan/background/todo/cron roots, file allowed dirs, MCP settings, and concrete CWD-derived caches. Register real cache invalidators instead of relying on an empty registry. Add a pluggable worktree analytics hook and emit keep/remove events after recounting.

implementation_subtasks.title: Support hook-based ExitWorktree keep/remove lifecycle
acceptance_criteria: Non-git WorktreeCreate hook success records an active hookBased worktree session.
ExitWorktree action='keep' for hookBased clears/restores session state while preserving the hook-created path.
ExitWorktree action='remove' calls WorktreeRemove with the worktree path and handles no-hook behavior according to TS.
Git worktree removal remains unchanged for non-hook sessions.
Tests use a fake bridge that records WorktreeCreate/WorktreeRemove calls and payloads.
implementation_subtasks.notes: Track hook-based worktree sessions in WorktreeState, including path/name/session metadata, and make ExitWorktree remove call WorktreeRemove through the configured bridge instead of git. EnterWorktree's hook branch should set active state and persisted session metadata the same way the git branch does.

implementation_subtasks.title: Add tmux session tracking and ExitWorktree tmux handling
acceptance_criteria: Keep returns tmuxSessionName in structured output and message includes the TS-style reattach guidance.
Remove invokes tmux kill-session for the stored session name before filesystem cleanup.
No tmux command is attempted when TmuxSessionName is empty.
Tmux failure is handled consistently with TS best-effort behavior.
implementation_subtasks.notes: Extend WorktreeState/persisted state with TmuxSessionName and provide an injectable tmux killer for tests. Keep should include tmuxSessionName and a reattach note in the structured message; remove should kill the tmux session before cleanup when a session name exists.

implementation_subtasks.title: Expose input-sensitive destructive metadata for ExitWorktree remove
acceptance_criteria: ExitWorktree keep is not classified destructive.
ExitWorktree remove is classified destructive before execution.
The classifier input for ExitWorktree is the action string, matching TS toAutoClassifierInput.
Existing deferred discovery metadata remains intact.
implementation_subtasks.notes: Add or reuse a Go tool metadata interface that can classify destructive input and auto-classifier input, then implement it for ExitWorktree so action='remove' is destructive and action='keep' is not. Wire the metadata where the loop/permission layer makes tool approval decisions.

implementation_subtasks.title: Make cleanup failure and partial-success behavior an explicit TS-parity decision
acceptance_criteria: git worktree remove failure behavior is covered by tests and either matches TS clearing/success semantics or is explicitly marked as an intentional divergence.
branch deletion failure behavior is covered by tests and has stable structured output fields.
A short delay or retry strategy around branch deletion is implemented if exact TS lock-release parity is selected.
State clearing after partial cleanup is deterministic and tested.
implementation_subtasks.notes: Align Go cleanup failure behavior with TS, or document and encode an intentional safer divergence. For exact parity, cleanup should best-effort log/report git remove and branch-delete failures while still clearing active session state and returning the structured remove result. If retaining Go's stricter errors, add an explicit parity-exception note and tests so future audits do not rediscover it.

implementation_subtasks.title: Tighten ExitWorktree input schema, descriptions, and conformance tests
acceptance_criteria: Unknown input keys are rejected for ExitWorktree, matching z.strictObject behavior.
discard_changes schema description mentions uncommitted files and unmerged/original-baseline commits.
Validation rejects invalid action before inactive-session handling.
Real git fixture tests cover clean, dirty, committed, unknown-baseline, discard true, structured output, and no-active cases.
implementation_subtasks.notes: Add strict-object support for schemas or ExitWorktree-specific unknown-field rejection, update discard_changes guidance to mention both uncommitted files and commits, and add focused conformance tests for schema text, unknown inputs, validation ordering, and real git remove guards.

risks: Some subtasks touch shared runtime surfaces; coordinate with foundation tasks to avoid incompatible local adapters.
non_goals: Do not make unrelated behavior changes outside this tool unless required by a listed dependency.
notes_for_assignee: Start by adding or updating parity fixtures, then implement the smallest vertical slice that makes a failing fixture pass. Keep TS evidence lines in comments or test names where useful.
